rows.read_by: claude-opus-5 reading the page's own TEXT LAYER with pdfplumber (no recognition): each page's money tokens are matched as `(?$n,nnn.nn)?`, their printed RIGHT EDGES clustered on THAT page, and every figure placed under the column whose cluster it falls in, so a fund that prints nothing in a column keeps that column ABSENT rather than shifting the next figure left. THE RULER IS MEASURED PER PAGE AND THE PAGES DISAGREE: the four right edges are 335.9/410.2/495.8/570.1 on p31, 334.7/408.2/492.8/566.2 on p32, 335.8/409.5/494.4/568.1 on p33, 336.1/410.0/494.9/568.7 on p34 and 336.6/410.8/496.1/570.3 on p35 -- reading one page with another page's ruler throws figures into the wrong column.
rows.proof: SPECIAL REVENUE FUNDS, FISCAL YEAR ENDING 6/30/16 -- the schedule the FY2016 annual town report prints across PDF pages 31, 33, 34 and 35. PROGRAM NAME | FORWARD 7/1/2015 | TOTAL RECEIPTS | TOTAL DISBURSEMENTS | BALANCE FWD 7/1/2016. 130 funds. ALL FOUR COLUMNS TIE TO THE CENT to the GRAND TOTAL the schedule prints on page 35: $2,704,480.72 / $6,543,358.01 / $6,074,216.03 / $3,173,622.70. AND PAGE 32 IS NOT IN THIS GROUP, DELIBERATELY: the report prints an extra, un-headed page between 31 and 33 that reprints 26 of page 33's funds and the first fund of page 34, figure for figure in all four columns. Including it puts the forward column $3,211.41 over the printed GRAND TOTAL; excluding it ties all four exactly, and excluding page 33 instead does NOT tie (short $1.97, the `Community Policing FY 97` row page 34 also carries). That is what establishes which printing the town counted. The reprint is read and published separately in `fy2016-p32-special-revenue-reprint.csv`. THE ROW IDENTITY THE SCHEDULE STATES -- forward + receipts - disbursements = balance carried forward -- HOLDS ON ALL 157 ROWS OF ALL FIVE PAGES, including the 27 reprinted ones, computed at read time. IT IS NOT DECLARED HERE BECAUSE verify_page_reads.py CANNOT EXPRESS IT: its grammar takes `a,b,c=d` (all added) or `a-b-c=d` (all subtracted after the first) and this identity is MIXED. Written `forward,receipts-disbursements=carried` the parser looks for a column literally named `forward,receipts`, finds none, and asserts `-disbursements = carried`, which fails on every row; storing disbursements negated would make it pass and would publish a figure the page does not print. So the group is proved on the printed GRAND TOTAL, which is the stronger half, and the row identity is recorded here as computed rather than asserted.

rows.reconciliation: page 36, the row `Grand Total`: appropriated_forward 11,120,094.93 vs printed 11,120,094.93 ; balance 6,744,697.27 vs printed 6,744,697.27 ; expended_encumbered_transferred 4,375,397.66 vs printed 4,375,397.66
rows.read_by: claude-opus-5 reading the page's OWN TEXT LAYER with pdfplumber -- the page carries no image, so these are the characters in the file and no recognition was involved. THE PAGE IS MIRRORED AND ROTATED IN ITS OWN TEXT LAYER, exactly as FY2014 page 34 and FY2015 page 34 are: every word reads backwards (`SDNUF TCEJORP LATIPAC`), the word ORDER within a label is reversed, and what scans as a run at constant `top` is a COLUMN of the printed table while a run at constant `x1` is a ROW. It renders mirrored as well as reading mirrored -- rasterised at 130 dpi and rotated 270 degrees the page is legible and was read that way too. THE ROW GRID IS MEASURED: the 54 distinct `x1` values cluster at a pitch of about 8.7pt with no cluster wider than 4pt, so every row is its own cluster and nothing is merged. THE THREE MONEY COLUMNS ARE NAMED FROM THE PRINTED HEADER, read off the rendered page: APPROPRIATED FORWARD (top 280-295), EXPENDED/ENCUMBERED/TRANSFERRED (top 120-135) and BALANCE (top 35-50); a narrow unlabelled column carries the flag `fwd` on 32 rows.
rows.proof: `CAPITAL PROJECT FUNDS FY 2016`, PDF page 36 of the FY2016 annual town report. 46 project rows in four `FYnn Capital Program` groups, plus the Grand Total. WHAT CLOSES: all THREE columns add down the 46 rows to the Grand Total the page itself prints -- $11,120,094.93 appropriated/forward, $4,375,397.66 expended/encumbered/transferred, $6,744,697.27 balance -- each to the CENT, and the Grand Total row is itself internally consistent (11,120,094.93 - 4,375,397.66 = 6,744,697.27). 45 of the 46 rows return appropriated/forward less expended as their printed balance. THE PAGE PRINTS A ROW WITH NO PURPOSE. Between the column header and `08/02 ATM Development of Cemeteries` the table rules a full row that carries `$25,000.00` in APPROPRIATED FORWARD and NOTHING ELSE -- no purpose, no article reference, no `fwd` flag, no expended figure and no balance. It was read off the rendered page, not inferred from the text layer. It is recorded here as its own row, `(no purpose printed)`, because that is what the document prints. AND IT IS WHY `Development of Cemeteries` IS ATTESTED. That row prints $1,019.01 forward and $35,229.38 expended against a printed balance of ($9,210.37); $1,019.01 - $35,229.38 is ($34,210.37), so the row as printed is out by exactly $25,000.00 -- the nameless row above it. The three column totals tie only when BOTH rows are counted, which is what establishes that the $25,000.00 is part of the schedule and not a stray. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW: that the $25,000.00 belongs to the Cemeteries project. The row is blank, the report says nothing about it, and `$25,000.00 exactly reconciles that row` is one explanation among others -- a cell whose label failed to print, a second article against the same project, and a separate project whose text was lost all fit the same evidence. Nothing here tests it. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the Town Accountant's capital project fund detail for FY2016, by article. ALSO NOTE, and it is not asserted either: `21 5/12 ATM Reconstruction of Summer Street (25%)` prints $6,502.30 forward and $6,502.30 balance and NO expended figure at all -- the cell is empty, not a zero -- so its identity closes here only because an absent part is read as nothing. FY2015 page 34 carries the same shape on `08/02 ATM Development of Cemeteries`.
